options.text: Use onion strips as an odour-based indicator and note how the smell changes in each liquid.
Use onion strips and conclude that the onion's smell change is what makes lemon juice acidic.
Use red litmus paper, because any coloured paper is the right tool when colour vision is difficult.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Leena cannot tell litmus colours apart clearly. Her teacher asks her to test lemon juice and soap solution using a change she can notice without relying on colour, and offers onion strips whose smell changes in acid or base, as well as red litmus paper.

part_answers.answer: An olfactory indicator works by a smell change, so it suits a task where colour is hard to judge; litmus still depends on colour.

teacher.key_rationale: When colour-based indicators are unsuitable, choose an olfactory indicator such as onion and watch the smell change. The smell change reports acid/base; it does not cause acidity. Litmus still needs colour reading.
